sections.title: Reshape the quadratic to fit a template

board_events.text: Reshape the quadratic to fit a template
A whole family of integrals reduces to a few templates whose answers are inverse-trig or log.
The skill isn't memorising dozens of results — it's reshaping any quadratic into a canonical shape.
$\sin^{-1}$, $\tan^{-1}$ and the log-forms are built for $a^2-x^2$, $a^2+x^2$, $x^2-a^2$.

board_events.text: In the shifted variable $X=x+\tfrac{b}{2}$, a messy quadratic becomes a clean $X^2+A^2$ shape.
Linear numerator over a quadratic? Split into (derivative-of-quadratic) + (constant) — two templates.

segments.text: <curious>Here's a whole zoo of integrals that all secretly answer to just a handful of templates.
A large family of integrals, anything with a quadratic in the denominator or under a root, reduces to a few standard templates whose answers are inverse-trig or logarithm functions.
So the skill here is not memorising dozens of results. It's learning to reshape any quadratic into one of a few canonical shapes.
Why reshape? Because arcsine, arctangent, and the log-forms are built for clean expressions like a squared minus x squared, a squared plus x squared, or x squared minus a squared.
A messy x squared plus b x plus c doesn't match any of those, until you complete the square, rewriting it as x plus b over two, squared, plus a constant.
Picture completing the square literally: you've got a square of side x and two thin strips of width b over two; add the missing little corner square and the whole thing becomes one perfect square.
In the shifted variable capital X equals x plus b over two, that messy quadratic is now a clean X squared plus A squared, exactly a template shape.
One more setup: if the numerator is linear over a quadratic, split it into a derivative-of-the-quadratic part plus a constant part. The two parts use different templates.
<curious>यह integrals का एक पूरा चिड़ियाघर है जो असल में बस कुछ ही templates को जवाब देता है।
एक बड़ा family, denominator में quadratic या root के नीचे कुछ भी, कुछ standard templates में सिमट जाता है, जिनके answers inverse-trig या logarithm functions हैं।
तो यहाँ skill दर्ज़नों results रटना नहीं है। यह किसी भी quadratic को कुछ canonical shapes में से एक में reshape करना सीखना है।
Reshape क्यों? क्योंकि arcsine, arctangent, और log-forms साफ़ expressions के लिए बने हैं जैसे a square minus x square, a square plus x square, या x square minus a square।
एक messy x square plus b x plus c इनमें से किसी से match नहीं करता, जब तक square complete न करो, उसे x plus b over two, squared, plus एक constant की तरह लिखकर।
Completing the square को सचमुच देखो: तुम्हारे पास x भुजा का एक square है और b over two चौड़ाई की दो पतली strips; बीच वाला छोटा corner square जोड़ दो और पूरी चीज़ एक perfect square बन जाती है।
Shifted variable capital X बराबर x plus b over two में, वो messy quadratic अब साफ़ X square plus A square है, बिलकुल एक template shape।
एक और setup: अगर numerator quadratic के ऊपर linear हो, उसे derivative-of-the-quadratic part plus constant part में split करो। दोनों parts अलग templates इस्तेमाल करते हैं।

sections.subtopic: Integrals of Special Forms (Quadratic Denominators & Roots)
sections.title: The core templates

board_events.text: The templates to recognise
Sign in the denominator picks the function: $+\to\tan^{-1}$, $-\to$ log-of-ratio. And $\sin^{-1}$ carries no $\tfrac{1}{a}$.
For $px+q$ over a quadratic: write $px+q = \lambda\,\tfrac{d}{dx}(\text{quad}) + \mu$; the $\lambda$-part gives log or root, the $\mu$-part a template.

segments.text: These are the templates to burn into memory. Every problem in this subtopic is completing the square, then matching one of these.
First: one over x squared plus a squared integrates to one over a, arctan x over a. The plus sign gives you arctan.
Change that plus to a minus: one over x squared minus a squared integrates to one over two a, log of the ratio x minus a over x plus a.
Under a root: one over root a squared minus x squared is arcsine x over a, and notice, no one-over-a factor out front.
The other two root forms both give a log: one over root x squared plus or minus a squared integrates to log of x plus that same root.
Then the square-root integrals themselves. Root a squared minus x squared integrates to x over two times the root, plus a squared over two times arcsine x over a.
And root x squared plus a squared integrates to x over two times the root, plus a squared over two times the log form. There's a matching result for x squared minus a squared.
The single most important reading: the sign in the denominator picks the function, plus gives arctan, minus gives a log ratio. And remember the arcsine form carries no one-over-a.
Finally, for a linear numerator p x plus q over a quadratic, write it as lambda times the derivative of the quadratic, plus mu. The lambda part gives a log or a root; the mu part is a pure template.
ये templates दिमाग में जमा लो। इस subtopic की हर problem है square complete करना, फिर इनमें से किसी से match करना।
पहला: one over x square plus a square integrate होकर one over a, arctan x over a. Plus sign तुम्हें arctan देता है।
उस plus को minus कर दो: one over x square minus a square integrate होकर one over two a, log of the ratio x minus a over x plus a।
Root के नीचे: one over root a square minus x square है arcsine x over a, और ध्यान दो, आगे कोई one-over-a factor नहीं।
बाकी दो root forms दोनों एक log देते हैं: one over root x square plus या minus a square integrate होकर log of x plus वही root।
फिर square-root integrals खुद। Root a square minus x square integrate होकर x over two times the root, plus a square over two times arcsine x over a।
और root x square plus a square integrate होकर x over two times the root, plus a square over two times log form। x square minus a square के लिए एक मिलता-जुलता result है।
सबसे important reading: denominator का sign function चुनता है, plus देता है arctan, minus देता है log ratio। और याद रखो arcsine form में कोई one-over-a नहीं।
आखिर में, quadratic के ऊपर linear numerator p x plus q के लिए, इसे lambda times the derivative of the quadratic, plus mu लिखो। Lambda part एक log या root देता है; mu part एक pure template है।

sections.subtopic: Integrals of Special Forms (Quadratic Denominators & Roots)
sections.title: Read the sign: arctan versus log

board_events.text: Example 1: a direct arctan
Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{x^2+9}$. Match $\int\frac{dx}{x^2+a^2}$ with $a=3$.
Example 2: a direct log ratio
Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{x^2-16}$. Match $\int\frac{dx}{x^2-a^2}$ with $a=4$, so $\tfrac{1}{2a}=\tfrac{1}{8}$.
Read the sign first: $x^2+a^2$ gives arctan; $x^2-a^2$ gives a log of a ratio.
Same-looking denominators, opposite answers — the plus/minus decides everything.

segments.text: Two lookups first, to lock in reading the sign.
We want the integral of one over x squared plus nine. Match the arctan template with a equals three.
So the answer is one-third arctan x over three, plus C. Clean.
Now change one symbol, a minus instead of a plus.
We want one over x squared minus sixteen. Match the log template with a equals four, so one over two a is one-eighth.
The answer is one-eighth log of the ratio x minus four over x plus four, plus C.
The whole game is reading the sign first. A plus in the denominator gives arctan; a minus gives a log of a ratio.
Two denominators that look almost identical produce completely different answers, the plus or minus decides everything, so read it before you write.
पहले दो lookups, sign पढ़ना पक्का करने के लिए।
हमें integral चाहिए one over x square plus nine का। arctan template को a equals three से match करो।
तो answer है one-third arctan x over three, plus C. साफ़।
अब एक symbol बदलो, plus की जगह minus।
हमें चाहिए one over x square minus sixteen। log template को a equals four से match करो, तो one over two a है one-eighth।
Answer है one-eighth log of the ratio x minus four over x plus four, plus C।
पूरा खेल है पहले sign पढ़ना। Denominator में plus देता है arctan; minus देता है log of a ratio।
दो denominators जो लगभग एक जैसे दिखते हैं, बिलकुल अलग answers देते हैं, plus या minus सब तय करता है, तो लिखने से पहले पढ़ो।

sections.subtopic: Integrals of Special Forms (Quadratic Denominators & Roots)
sections.title: Completing the square; linear over a root

board_events.text: Example 3: complete the square
Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{x^2+4x+13}$. Complete the square: $x^2+4x+13=(x+2)^2+9$.
Example 4: a linear numerator over a root
Evaluate $\int \frac{2x+3}{\sqrt{x^2+4x+8}}\,dx$. Since $\tfrac{d}{dx}(x^2+4x+8)=2x+4$, write $2x+3=(2x+4)-1$.
Leftover: $x^2+4x+8=(x+2)^2+4$, so $\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(x+2)^2+4}}=\ln\left|(x+2)+\sqrt{x^2+4x+8}\right|$.
Split a linear numerator into (derivative-part) + (constant-part) — the master key for (linear)/(quadratic).

segments.text: Now the real skill: reshaping before matching.
We want one over x squared plus four x plus thirteen. Complete the square: that denominator is x plus two, all squared, plus nine.
With capital X equal to x plus two, it's the arctan template with a equals three, one-third arctan X over three.
Convert back: the answer is one-third arctan of x plus two over three, plus C.
<curious>Now the boss level, a linear numerator sitting over the root of a quadratic.
We want two x plus three, over root x squared plus four x plus eight. The derivative of the inside is two x plus four, so write two x plus three as two x plus four, minus one.
The two x plus four part is exactly the derivative of the inside, so it integrates by the f prime over root f rule to two times the root.
The leftover minus one part: complete the square to x plus two squared plus four, and it becomes log of x plus two, plus the root.
Combine: two times the root, minus log of x plus two plus the root, plus C.
Bank this move, splitting a linear numerator into a derivative part plus a constant part. It's the master key for every linear-over-quadratic integral, root or no root.
अब असली skill: match करने से पहले reshape करना।
हमें चाहिए one over x square plus four x plus thirteen। Square complete करो: वो denominator है x plus two, पूरा squared, plus nine।
Capital X बराबर x plus two के साथ, यह arctan template है a equals three के साथ, one-third arctan X over three।
वापस बदलो: answer है one-third arctan of x plus two over three, plus C।
<curious>अब boss level, quadratic के root के ऊपर बैठा एक linear numerator।
हमें चाहिए two x plus three, बटा root x square plus four x plus eight। अंदर का derivative है two x plus four, तो two x plus three को two x plus four, minus one लिखो।
Two x plus four वाला हिस्सा ठीक अंदर का derivative है, तो यह f prime over root f rule से integrate होकर two times the root बनता है।
बचा हुआ minus one हिस्सा: square complete करके x plus two squared plus four, और यह बन जाता है log of x plus two, plus the root।
जोड़ो: two times the root, minus log of x plus two plus the root, plus C।
यह move जमा लो, linear numerator को derivative part plus constant part में तोड़ना। यह हर linear-over-quadratic integral की master key है, root हो या न हो।

sections.subtopic: Integrals of Special Forms (Quadratic Denominators & Roots)
sections.title: Special-form pitfalls: three binary checks

board_events.text: Three binary checks pin the template
$x^2+a^2$ (arctan) vs $x^2-a^2$ (log): the denominator's sign picks the function. Read it first.
The $\tfrac{1}{a}$ factor: $\int\frac{dx}{x^2+a^2}$ has it; $\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{a^2-x^2}}=\sin^{-1}\tfrac{x}{a}$ has none.
Numerator $x$ vs $1$: numerator $x$ goes to a log via $f'/f$; a constant numerator goes to arctan or arcsin.
Any $x^2+bx+c$ must be reshaped by completing the square before a template applies.
Check one — sign: log or arctan? Check two — root present: arcsin or log-root? Check three — numerator $x$ or $1$?
Three binary checks pin the template before you write a single symbol.

segments.text: This subtopic rewards a quick triage. Three yes-or-no checks decide the whole answer.
Check the denominator's sign first. x squared plus a squared gives arctan; x squared minus a squared gives a log of a ratio. Same-looking forms, opposite answers.
Watch the one-over-a factor. The arctan template carries a one-over-a out front, but the arcsine template, one over root a squared minus x squared, carries none. Mixing these up is a classic slip.
Look at the numerator. If it's an x, you're heading to a log through the f prime over f pattern. If it's a constant, you're heading to arctan or arcsine. Same denominator, different problems.
And never forget to complete the square. Any x squared plus b x plus c has to be reshaped before any template applies.
So run three checks. One: the sign, log or arctan? Two: is there a root, arcsine or log-root? Three: numerator x or one?
The board shows the chain: sign, then root, then numerator.
<whisper>Those three binary checks pin the exact template before you write a single symbol.
यह subtopic एक जल्दी triage को reward करता है। तीन हाँ-या-ना checks पूरा answer तय करते हैं।
पहले denominator का sign check करो। x square plus a square देता है arctan; x square minus a square देता है log of a ratio। एक जैसे दिखने वाले forms, उल्टे answers।
One-over-a factor को देखो। arctan template आगे one-over-a रखता है, पर arcsine template, one over root a square minus x square, कोई नहीं रखता। इन्हें मिलाना classic slip है।
Numerator को देखो। अगर वो x है, तो तुम f prime over f pattern से log की तरफ़ जा रहे हो। अगर constant है, तो arctan या arcsine की तरफ़। Same denominator, अलग problems।
और square complete करना कभी मत भूलो। किसी भी x square plus b x plus c को template लगाने से पहले reshape करना ज़रूरी है।
तो तीन checks चलाओ। एक: sign, log या arctan? दो: root है क्या, arcsine या log-root? तीन: numerator x या one?
Board chain दिखाता है: sign, फिर root, फिर numerator।
<whisper>वो तीन binary checks एक भी symbol लिखने से पहले exact template पिन कर देते हैं।

sections.title: Partial fractions: addition run in reverse

board_events.text: Partial fractions: addition run in reverse
Some rationals like $\frac{1}{(x-1)(x+2)}$ have no direct integral — no single substitution simplifies them.
Break one complicated fraction into a sum of simpler ones, each integrating to a log or arctan.

board_events.caption: One combined fraction, itemised into simple pieces.

board_events.text: Need a proper fraction (numerator degree < denominator degree). If improper, divide first.
The denominator must be factorised; each factor type gets its own partial-fraction template.
It's literally the addition of fractions, run backwards to recover the unknown numerators.

segments.text: <curious>What do you do with a fraction that no substitution will simplify?
Take one over x minus one, times x plus two. There's no single substitution that cracks it, and it's not in any table.
The fix is to break that one complicated fraction into a sum of simpler fractions, each of which integrates cleanly to a log or an arctan.
So we claim it equals A over x minus one, plus B over x plus two, for some constants A and B we'll find.
Think of a restaurant handing your table one combined bill; partial fractions is itemising it, so each diner's share is easy to pay, that is, easy to integrate.
The one precondition: you need a proper fraction, numerator degree below denominator degree. If it's improper, do polynomial long division first.
And the denominator must be fully factorised, because each type of factor gets its own partial-fraction template.
At heart it's just the addition of fractions run in reverse: given the combined fraction, recover the separate numerators.
<curious>ऐसे fraction का क्या करोगे जिसे कोई substitution simplify नहीं करेगा?
लो one over x minus one, times x plus two। कोई एक substitution इसे नहीं तोड़ता, और यह किसी table में नहीं।
इलाज है उस एक जटिल fraction को simpler fractions के sum में तोड़ना, जिनमें से हर एक साफ़ log या arctan में integrate होता है।
तो हम कहते हैं यह बराबर है A over x minus one, plus B over x plus two, कुछ constants A और B के लिए जो हम निकालेंगे।
सोचो restaurant तुम्हारी table को एक combined bill देता है; partial fractions उसे itemise करना है, ताकि हर diner का हिस्सा pay करना आसान हो, यानी integrate करना आसान।
एक precondition: proper fraction चाहिए, numerator degree denominator degree से कम। Improper हो, तो पहले polynomial long division करो।
और denominator पूरी तरह factorise होना चाहिए, क्योंकि हर type के factor को अपना partial-fraction template मिलता है।
मूल में यह बस fractions का addition उल्टा चलाना है: combined fraction से अलग numerators वापस निकालो।

board_events.text: One term per factor
Each term then integrates: linear to a log, repeated to a power, quadratic to a log plus an arctan.
Cover-up (distinct linear): to find the numerator over $(x-r)$, delete that factor and set $x=r$.
Solve constants by substituting roots (fast) or by comparing coefficients (for repeated/quadratic).

segments.text: The decomposition follows one rule: one partial fraction per factor, matched to the factor's type.
A plain linear factor a x plus b gets a single constant over it, A over a x plus b.
A repeated linear factor, a x plus b squared, needs two terms: A over the factor, plus B over the factor squared.
An irreducible quadratic factor takes a linear numerator on top: A x plus B, over that quadratic.
Once split, each term integrates predictably: a linear factor gives a log, a repeated factor gives a power, and a quadratic gives a log plus an arctan.
Note the repeated case explicitly: one over x minus a, squared, integrates to minus one over x minus a, a power, not a log.
For distinct linear factors, the fastest trick is cover-up: to get the numerator over x minus r, delete that factor from the original and set x equal to r.
In general, find the constants either by substituting the roots, quick, or by comparing coefficients, which you'll need for repeated or quadratic factors.
Decomposition एक rule मानता है: हर factor पर एक partial fraction, factor के type से match।
एक plain linear factor a x plus b को उसके ऊपर एक single constant मिलता है, A over a x plus b।
एक repeated linear factor, a x plus b squared, को दो terms चाहिए: A over the factor, plus B over the factor squared।
एक irreducible quadratic factor ऊपर linear numerator लेता है: A x plus B, बटा वो quadratic।
Split होने के बाद, हर term predictable तरीके से integrate होता है: linear factor देता है log, repeated factor देता है power, और quadratic देता है log plus arctan।
Repeated case को साफ़ नोट करो: one over x minus a, squared, integrate होकर minus one over x minus a, एक power, log नहीं।
Distinct linear factors के लिए सबसे तेज़ trick है cover-up: x minus r के ऊपर numerator पाने के लिए, original से वो factor हटाओ और x को r रखो।
आम तौर पर, constants या तो roots रखकर निकालो, जल्दी, या coefficients compare करके, जो repeated या quadratic factors के लिए चाहिए।

board_events.text: Example 1: two distinct linear factors
Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{(x-1)(x+2)}$. Cover-up: $A=\tfrac{1}{3}$ at $x=1$, $B=-\tfrac{1}{3}$ at $x=-2$.
Example 2: cover-up with a linear numerator
Evaluate $\int \frac{3x+1}{(x+1)(x-2)}\,dx$. Over $(x+1)$, $x=-1\to\tfrac{2}{3}$; over $(x-2)$, $x=2\to\tfrac{7}{3}$.
Cover-up finds each constant in one substitution — no system of equations.

segments.text: Let's see the cover-up shortcut in action on two distinct linear factors.
We want one over x minus one, times x plus two. By cover-up: delete x minus one and set x to one, giving A equals one-third; delete x plus two and set x to minus two, giving B equals minus one-third.
So the fraction splits as one-third over x minus one, minus one-third over x plus two.
Each piece is a log, and combining them gives one-third log of the ratio x minus one over x plus two, plus C.
<excited>The same trick handles a linear numerator too, just as fast.
We want three x plus one, over x plus one times x minus two. Cover-up over x plus one: set x to minus one, and the rest gives two-thirds. Over x minus two: set x to two, giving seven-thirds.
So the integral is two-thirds log mod x plus one, plus seven-thirds log mod x minus two, plus C.
The payoff: cover-up finds each constant in a single substitution, with no system of equations to solve.
चलो cover-up shortcut को दो distinct linear factors पर काम करते देखें।
हमें चाहिए one over x minus one, times x plus two। Cover-up से: x minus one हटाओ और x को one रखो, तो A बराबर one-third; x plus two हटाओ और x को minus two रखो, तो B बराबर minus one-third।
तो fraction split होता है one-third over x minus one, minus one-third over x plus two।
हर piece एक log है, और इन्हें जोड़ने पर मिलता है one-third log of the ratio x minus one over x plus two, plus C।
<excited>यही trick एक linear numerator को भी सँभालता है, उतना ही तेज़।
हमें चाहिए three x plus one, बटा x plus one times x minus two। x plus one पर cover-up: x को minus one रखो, बाकी देता है two-thirds। x minus two पर: x को two रखो, तो seven-thirds।
तो integral है two-thirds log mod x plus one, plus seven-thirds log mod x minus two, plus C।
फ़ायदा: cover-up हर constant एक ही substitution में निकाल देता है, कोई system of equations हल नहीं करनी।

board_events.text: Example 3: a repeated linear factor
Evaluate $\int \frac{x}{(x-1)^2(x+1)}\,dx$. Template: $\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{C}{x+1}$.
Clear denominators; $x=1\Rightarrow B=\tfrac{1}{2}$; $x=-1\Rightarrow C=-\tfrac{1}{4}$; compare $x^2\Rightarrow A=\tfrac{1}{4}$.
Example 4: an improper fraction
Evaluate $\int \frac{x^3}{x^2+1}\,dx$. Degree $3\ge 2$ — divide first: $\frac{x^3}{x^2+1}=x-\frac{x}{x^2+1}$.
The second piece is an $f'/f$ form — numerator $x$ is half the derivative of $x^2+1$.
Always test degree first — skipping division on an improper fraction is the top way this goes wrong.

segments.text: Now a repeated factor, where the template grows an extra term.
We want x over x minus one squared, times x plus one. Because x minus one is repeated, the template needs A over x minus one, plus B over x minus one squared, plus C over x plus one.
Clear the denominators. Setting x to one gives B equals one-half; setting x to minus one gives C equals minus one-quarter; and comparing the x squared coefficients gives A equals one-quarter.
So the integral is one-quarter log mod x minus one, minus one-half times one over x minus one, minus one-quarter log mod x plus one.
Tidy it up: one-quarter log of the ratio x minus one over x plus one, minus one over two times x minus one, plus C.
<curious>Now the trap that catches everyone, an improper fraction.
We want x cubed over x squared plus one. The numerator's degree, three, is at least the denominator's, so you must divide first: it becomes x minus x over x squared plus one.
Integrate each piece: x squared over two, minus one-half log of x squared plus one, plus C.
That second piece is an f prime over f form, the numerator x is exactly half the derivative of x squared plus one.
The rule: always test the degree first. Skipping the division on an improper fraction is the single most common way this problem goes wrong.
अब एक repeated factor, जहाँ template एक extra term उगाता है।
हमें चाहिए x over x minus one squared, times x plus one। चूँकि x minus one repeated है, template को चाहिए A over x minus one, plus B over x minus one squared, plus C over x plus one।
Denominators clear करो। x को one रखने पर B बराबर one-half; x को minus one रखने पर C बराबर minus one-quarter; और x square coefficients compare करने पर A बराबर one-quarter।
तो integral है one-quarter log mod x minus one, minus one-half times one over x minus one, minus one-quarter log mod x plus one।
इसे साफ़ करो: one-quarter log of the ratio x minus one over x plus one, minus one over two times x minus one, plus C।
<curious>अब वो trap जो सबको पकड़ता है, एक improper fraction।
हमें चाहिए x cube over x square plus one। Numerator की degree, three, denominator से कम नहीं, तो पहले divide करना ज़रूरी है: यह बनता है x minus x over x square plus one।
हर piece integrate करो: x square बटा two, minus one-half log of x square plus one, plus C।
वो दूसरा piece एक f prime over f form है, numerator x ठीक x square plus one के derivative का आधा है।
Rule: हमेशा पहले degree test करो। Improper fraction पर division छोड़ना इस problem के गलत होने का सबसे common तरीका है।

board_events.text: Partial-fraction traps
Numerator degree $\ge$ denominator degree? Divide first. Forcing partial fractions on an improper fraction gives wrong constants.
A repeated factor $(x-a)^2$ needs both $\frac{A}{x-a}$ and $\frac{B}{(x-a)^2}$ — not just one.
An irreducible quadratic takes a linear numerator $Ax+B$; a linear factor takes a constant $A$.
Combining logs: $\ln|a|-\ln|b|=\ln|a/b|$ — track which factor is on top.
For distinct linear factors, skip the linear system — use cover-up, one substitution per constant.
Reserve coefficient-comparison for repeated or quadratic factors, where cover-up alone can't finish.

segments.text: Partial fractions has four reliable traps. Clear them and the method is mechanical.
First and biggest: if the numerator's degree is at least the denominator's, divide first. Forcing partial fractions onto an improper fraction produces wrong constants every time.
Second: a repeated factor, x minus a squared, needs both terms, A over x minus a, and B over x minus a squared. Writing only one is a guaranteed error.
Third: match the numerator to the factor. An irreducible quadratic takes a linear numerator, A x plus B; a linear factor takes just a constant A.
Fourth, a sign check when combining logs: log mod a minus log mod b is log of a over b. Keep track of which factor ends up on top.
The efficiency tip: for distinct linear factors, don't set up a linear system at all, cover-up gives each constant in one substitution.
The board lays out the workflow: improper means divide, then factor, template, solve, integrate.
<whisper>Save coefficient-comparison for repeated or quadratic factors, where cover-up alone can't finish the job.
Partial fractions के चार भरोसेमंद traps हैं। इन्हें साफ़ कर दो और method mechanical हो जाता है।
पहला और सबसे बड़ा: अगर numerator की degree denominator से कम नहीं, तो पहले divide करो। Improper fraction पर partial fractions थोपने से हर बार गलत constants आते हैं।
दूसरा: एक repeated factor, x minus a squared, को दोनों terms चाहिए, A over x minus a, और B over x minus a squared। सिर्फ़ एक लिखना पक्की गलती है।
तीसरा: numerator को factor से match करो। एक irreducible quadratic linear numerator लेता है, A x plus B; एक linear factor बस एक constant A।
चौथा, logs जोड़ते समय sign check: log mod a minus log mod b है log of a over b। ध्यान रखो कौन सा factor ऊपर आता है।
Efficiency tip: distinct linear factors के लिए linear system बनाओ ही मत, cover-up हर constant एक substitution में देता है।
Board workflow रखता है: improper मतलब divide, फिर factor, template, solve, integrate।
<whisper>Coefficient-comparison को repeated या quadratic factors के लिए बचाओ, जहाँ अकेला cover-up काम पूरा नहीं करता।

sections.title: Integration by parts: the product rule reversed

board_events.text: Integration by parts: the product rule reversed
Substitution needs a function times its own derivative. But what about $x\cos x$ or $xe^x$?
Parts is built for products of two unrelated functions — the reverse of the product rule.

board_events.caption: ILATE: the earlier a function appears, the better it is as u.
board_events.svg: <svg font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" viewBox="0 0 360 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="360" height="240" fill="#ffffff"/><defs><marker id="il" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="#e53e3e"/></marker></defs><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#2b6cb0"><rect x="95" y="20" width="200" height="34" rx="5" fill="#ebf8ff" stroke="#2b6cb0"/><text x="195" y="42" text-anchor="middle">I : Inverse-trig</text><rect x="95" y="60" width="200" height="34" rx="5" fill="#ebf8ff" stroke="#2b6cb0"/><text x="195" y="82" text-anchor="middle">L : Logarithm</text><rect x="95" y="100" width="200" height="34" rx="5" fill="#ebf8ff" stroke="#2b6cb0"/><text x="195" y="122" text-anchor="middle">A : Algebraic</text><rect x="95" y="140" width="200" height="34" rx="5" fill="#ebf8ff" stroke="#2b6cb0"/><text x="195" y="162" text-anchor="middle">T : Trigonometric</text><rect x="95" y="180" width="200" height="34" rx="5" fill="#ebf8ff" stroke="#2b6cb0"/><text x="195" y="202" text-anchor="middle">E : Exponential</text></g><line x1="55" y1="30" x2="55" y2="205" stroke="#e53e3e" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#il)"/><text x="28" y="120" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#e53e3e" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90 28 120)">choose u from the top</text></svg>

board_events.text: Differentiate the 'hard' factor $u$, integrate the 'easy' one — hoping the new integral is simpler.
A bad choice makes $\int v\,du$ harder — then swap your $u$ and $dv$.
Some integrals like $\int e^x\sin x$ cycle back after two applications — then solve algebraically.

segments.text: <curious>Substitution was for a function tangled up with its own derivative. What do we do with a plain product of two unrelated functions?
Think of x times cosine x, or x times e to the x. There's no inner function and its derivative to exploit, so substitution has nothing to grab.
Integration by parts is the tool built exactly for products. It's the reverse of the product rule for differentiation.
The formula trades one integral for another: the integral of u d v equals u v, minus the integral of v d u.

Which factor should be u? Use ILATE, Inverse-trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential. The earlier a function sits on that ladder, the better it is as u, because differentiating it simplifies things.
The plan is to differentiate the hard factor u down to something simpler, integrate the easy factor, and hope the new integral is easier than the one you started with.
If your choice makes the new integral harder instead, that's the signal to swap: make the other factor u.
And a few integrals, like e to the x times sine x, cycle back to themselves after two rounds of parts, at which point you solve for the integral algebraically.
<curious>Substitution उस function के लिए था जो अपने ही derivative में उलझा हो। दो unrelated functions के plain product का क्या करें?
सोचो x times cosine x, या x times e to the x। यहाँ कोई inner function और उसका derivative नहीं जिसे exploit करें, तो substitution के पास पकड़ने को कुछ नहीं।
Integration by parts ठीक products के लिए बना tool है। यह differentiation के product rule का उल्टा है।
Formula एक integral को दूसरे से बदल देता है: integral of u d v बराबर u v, minus integral of v d u।
कौन सा factor u हो? ILATE इस्तेमाल करो, Inverse-trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential। जो function इस ladder पर जितना पहले, उतना अच्छा u, क्योंकि उसे differentiate करना चीज़ें simple करता है।
Plan है hard factor u को differentiate करके कुछ simpler बनाना, easy factor को integrate करना, और उम्मीद करना कि नया integral शुरुआत से आसान हो।
अगर तुम्हारा choice नया integral और मुश्किल बना दे, यही signal है swap का: दूसरे factor को u बनाओ।
और कुछ integrals, जैसे e to the x times sine x, दो parts के rounds बाद खुद पर लौट आते हैं, तब integral को algebraically हल करते हैं।

sections.title: The parts formula, ILATE, and standard results

board_events.text: The formula and its two golden results

board_events.latex: \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du \qquad \int u\,v'\,dx = uv - \int u'\,v\,dx

board_events.text: ILATE picks u: Inverse-trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential — earlier means differentiate it.

board_events.latex: \int e^{ax}\sin bx\,dx = \frac{e^{ax}(a\sin bx - b\cos bx)}{a^2+b^2} + C
\int e^{ax}\cos bx\,dx = \frac{e^{ax}(a\cos bx + b\sin bx)}{a^2+b^2} + C

board_events.text: Derivation: integrate the product rule $(uv)'=u'v+uv'$ and rearrange for $\int uv'\,dx$.
See $e^x$ times a sum? Check if the second term is the derivative of the first — then jump to $e^x f(x)$.

segments.text: Here's the formula and the two high-value results that turn hard problems into one-liners.
The core formula: the integral of u d v equals u v minus the integral of v d u. Equivalently, differentiate u, integrate v prime, and subtract the leftover integral.
To choose u, use ILATE, Inverse-trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential. Whichever comes earlier on that list is the one you differentiate.
The golden shortcut: the integral of e to the x times f plus f prime is simply e to the x times f, plus C.
Two cycling results worth memorising: the integral of e to the a x sine b x is e to the a x, times a sine b x minus b cosine b x, all over a squared plus b squared.
And its partner: the integral of e to the a x cosine b x is e to the a x, times a cosine b x plus b sine b x, over a squared plus b squared.
Where does the main formula come from? Just integrate the product rule, u v prime plus u prime v, and rearrange to isolate the integral of u v prime.
Train this reflex: whenever you see e to the x times a sum, check if the second term is the derivative of the first. If so, jump straight to e to the x times f.
यह रहा formula और वो दो high-value results जो मुश्किल problems को one-liner बना देते हैं।
Core formula: integral of u d v बराबर u v minus integral of v d u। यानी u को differentiate करो, v prime को integrate करो, और बचा हुआ integral घटाओ।
u चुनने के लिए ILATE इस्तेमाल करो, Inverse-trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential। इस list में जो पहले आए, उसी को differentiate करो।
Golden shortcut: integral of e to the x times f plus f prime बस e to the x times f, plus C है।
याद रखने लायक दो cycling results: integral of e to the a x sine b x है e to the a x, times a sine b x minus b cosine b x, बटा a square plus b square।
और इसका partner: integral of e to the a x cosine b x है e to the a x, times a cosine b x plus b sine b x, बटा a square plus b square।
मुख्य formula कहाँ से आता है? बस product rule integrate करो, u v prime plus u prime v, और u v prime के integral को अलग करने के लिए rearrange करो।
यह reflex जमाओ: जब भी e to the x times a sum दिखे, check करो कि दूसरा term पहले का derivative है क्या। हो, तो सीधे e to the x times f पर कूदो।

sections.title: Parts basics: ILATE and the times-one trick

board_events.text: Example 1: pick u by ILATE
Evaluate $\int x\cos x\,dx$. Algebraic before Trig, so $u=x$, $dv=\cos x\,dx$; then $du=dx$, $v=\sin x$.

board_events.latex: \int x\cos x\,dx = x\sin x - \int \sin x\,dx = x\sin x + \cos x + C

board_events.text: Example 2: the lone ln x trick
Evaluate $\int \ln x\,dx$. Treat it as $\ln x\cdot 1$: $u=\ln x$, $dv=1\,dx$, so $du=\tfrac{1}{x}dx$, $v=x$.

board_events.latex: \int \ln x\,dx = x\ln x - \int x\cdot\frac{1}{x}\,dx = x\ln x - x + C

board_events.text: A lone $\ln x$ or $\tan^{-1}x$ pairs with an invisible $\times 1$, then parts applies.
ILATE: differentiate the earlier function — choosing $u=e^x$ over an algebraic term makes it harder.

segments.text: Let's apply parts cleanly. First, a textbook product.
We want the integral of x cosine x. On the ILATE ladder, Algebraic comes before Trig, so let u be x and d v be cosine x d x. Then d u is d x, and v is sine x.
Plug into the formula: x sine x, minus the integral of sine x. That's x sine x plus cosine x, plus C.
<curious>Now a favourite trick, integrating a lone logarithm.
We want the integral of log x. There's only one function, so treat it as log x times an invisible one. Then u is log x, d v is one d x, so d u is one over x d x and v is x.
The formula gives x log x, minus the integral of x times one over x, which is just the integral of one. So the answer is x log x, minus x, plus C.
That's the move for any lone log x or arctan x: pair it with a times one, then apply parts.
And the ILATE reminder: always differentiate the earlier function. Choosing e to the x as u over an algebraic term would only make the new integral harder.
चलो parts साफ़ लगाएँ। पहले, एक textbook product।
हमें integral चाहिए x cosine x का। ILATE ladder पर Algebraic, Trig से पहले आता है, तो u को x और d v को cosine x d x मानो। तो d u है d x, और v है sine x।
Formula में रखो: x sine x, minus integral of sine x। यह है x sine x plus cosine x, plus C।
<curious>अब एक पसंदीदा trick, एक अकेले logarithm को integrate करना।
हमें integral चाहिए log x का। सिर्फ़ एक function है, तो इसे log x times एक invisible one मानो। तो u है log x, d v है one d x, तो d u है one over x d x और v है x।
Formula देता है x log x, minus integral of x times one over x, जो बस integral of one है। तो answer है x log x, minus x, plus C।
यही move है किसी भी अकेले log x या arctan x के लिए: उसे times one के साथ pair करो, फिर parts लगाओ।
और ILATE reminder: हमेशा पहले वाले function को differentiate करो। e to the x को u चुनना, algebraic term के बजाय, बस नया integral और मुश्किल कर देता।

sections.title: The cycling integral and the e-to-x times (f + f prime) shortcut

board_events.text: Example 3: an integral that cycles
Evaluate $I=\int e^x\sin x\,dx$. Parts gives $I = e^x\sin x - \int e^x\cos x\,dx$.
Parts again on the new integral: $\int e^x\cos x\,dx = e^x\cos x + I$.

board_events.latex: I = e^x\sin x - (e^x\cos x + I) \;\Rightarrow\; 2I = e^x(\sin x - \cos x)

board_events.text: Example 4: spot e-to-x times (f + f prime)
Evaluate $\int e^x\left(\tfrac{1}{x}-\tfrac{1}{x^2}\right)dx$. Let $f=\tfrac{1}{x}$, so $f'=-\tfrac{1}{x^2}$ — exactly $e^x[f+f']$.
Recognising $e^x[f+f']$ turns a hard-looking integral into a one-line answer — always check for it.

segments.text: Here's an integral that seems to loop forever, until you use the loop to your advantage.
We want capital I, the integral of e to the x sine x. One round of parts gives I equals e to the x sine x, minus the integral of e to the x cosine x.
Apply parts again to that new integral, and it comes out to e to the x cosine x, plus our original I back again.
Substitute: I equals e to the x sine x, minus the quantity e to the x cosine x plus I. Move the I over, and two I equals e to the x times sine x minus cosine x.
Divide by two: the integral is e to the x times sine x minus cosine x, all over two, plus C. We solved for I like an algebraic unknown.
<excited>Now the shortcut that makes a scary integral collapse in one line.

We want the integral of e to the x times one over x minus one over x squared. Let f be one over x; then f prime is minus one over x squared, so the integrand is exactly e to the x times f plus f prime.
By the standard result, the answer is just e to the x times f, that is, e to the x over x, plus C.
So always check for the e to the x times f-plus-f-prime pattern. Recognising it turns a hard-looking integral into a one-line answer.
यह एक integral है जो हमेशा loop करता लगता है, जब तक तुम उस loop को अपने फ़ायदे में न लगाओ।
हमें चाहिए capital I, integral of e to the x sine x। Parts का एक round देता है I बराबर e to the x sine x, minus integral of e to the x cosine x।
उस नए integral पर फिर parts लगाओ, और वह निकलता है e to the x cosine x, plus हमारा original I फिर से।
रखो: I बराबर e to the x sine x, minus पूरी quantity e to the x cosine x plus I। I को दूसरी तरफ़ ले जाओ, और two I बराबर e to the x times sine x minus cosine x।
Two से भाग दो: integral है e to the x times sine x minus cosine x, बटा two, plus C। हमने I को एक algebraic unknown की तरह हल किया।
<excited>अब वो shortcut जो एक डरावने integral को एक line में समेट देता है।
हमें चाहिए integral of e to the x times one over x minus one over x square। मान लो f है one over x; तो f prime है minus one over x square, यानी integrand ठीक e to the x times f plus f prime है।
Standard result से, answer बस e to the x times f है, यानी e to the x over x, plus C।
तो हमेशा e to the x times f-plus-f-prime pattern check करो। इसे पहचानना एक hard दिखने वाले integral को one-line answer बना देता है।

board_events.text: Integration-by-parts traps
Choose $u$ and $dv$ by ILATE — differentiate the earlier function. The wrong split makes $\int v\,du$ harder.
Sign care: $v=\int\sin x = -\cos x$. Carry that minus through both terms of the formula.
For $\int e^x\sin x$, after two applications the original reappears — solve for it, don't loop forever.
See $e^x$ times a sum? Check whether the second term is the derivative of the first — then use the shortcut.
A lone $\ln x$, $\tan^{-1}x$, or $\sin^{-1}x$? Pair with an invisible $\times 1$ and apply parts.
Test the $f+f'$ pattern before grinding through parts — it converts many hard problems into instant answers.

segments.text: Parts rewards a few habits. Get these right and the method rarely fights back.
First, choose u and d v by ILATE, differentiate the earlier function. The wrong split makes the new integral, v d u, harder than the one you started with.
Second, mind the sign. Integrating sine gives minus cosine, so v is minus cosine x, and you must carry that minus through both terms of the formula.
Third, remember the cycling trick. For e to the x sine x, after two applications the original integral reappears; solve for it algebraically instead of looping forever.
Fourth, watch for e to the x times a sum. Check whether the second term is the derivative of the first, if so, the shortcut gives the answer instantly.
And for a lone log x, arctan x, or arcsine x, pair it with an invisible times one, then apply parts as usual.
The board captures the two shortcuts: e to the x times f plus f prime gives e to the x times f; and a lone log or inverse-trig pairs with a times one.
<whisper>Before grinding through parts on any e to the x integral, test the f plus f prime pattern first, it turns many hard problems into instant answers.

तीसरी, cycling trick याद रखो। e to the x sine x के लिए, दो applications बाद original integral लौट आता है; उसे loop करने के बजाय algebraically हल करो।
चौथी, e to the x times a sum के लिए सतर्क रहो। Check करो कि दूसरा term पहले का derivative है क्या, हो, तो shortcut तुरंत answer देता है।
और एक अकेले log x, arctan x, या arcsine x के लिए, उसे invisible times one के साथ pair करो, फिर हमेशा की तरह parts लगाओ।
